translation.proposition_plain_english: For any finite nonempty collection of directions, positive number of state components, compatible finite-volume geometry, directional line coordinates, controlled one-dimensional method families and sequence of their realizations, assume that every executed stage has an admitted actual state and admitted reference cell means, that the reference already obeys the directional cell integral conservation law, and that the initial error, selected stability amplification, two numerical-versus-physical face errors and interstage reference mismatch satisfy the stated bounds. If the finite schedule visits every direction, then all the displayed structural, one-dimensional accuracy, chronological composition, line-realization, summed flux-balance, line-locality, conditional cell-accuracy and physical-balance statements hold, and the error at every cell through the terminal stage is bounded by the scalar recurrence B_{n+1}=a_n B_n+b_n+s_n. In addition, whenever the abstract geometry has the specified Cartesian measure and flux compatibility, cell volumes and means have the stated product formulas and lifted one-dimensional conservative fields satisfy the stated face-flux and all-time cell-balance identities. The result is conditional on these supplied objects and estimates; it does not construct them or establish convergence of the multidimensional trajectory to a solution of an independently specified multidimensional PDE.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: m>0 excludes zero-component states, and |D|>0 excludes an empty direction set. The cell-partition structure requires Nonempty Cell, and physical data give each cell positive finite measure. Thus cellwise assumptions and conclusions are not vacuous through an empty cell type.

The coordinate and face maps, together with nonempty D and Cell, force Line and Face to be nonempty. The schedule coverage implies S≥|D|≥1. It requires neither a prescribed order nor exactly one occurrence of each direction.

Every selected duration is positive because it equals a family time step on every line. All physical cell volumes and grid widths are positive, so the actual update and time-average denominators cannot vanish.

The mesh parameter tends to zero only along each separate family's refinement index. The executed method levels need not increase with stage number and need not tend to infinity. The theorem fixes a finite stage horizon.

The family has nonempty active windows of at least two cells and nonempty fixed interior coverage. Its admission predicate is otherwise arbitrary. Initial projections become admitted eventually only for references satisfying the qualifying regularity, conservation and state conditions.

No qualifying one-dimensional reference is asserted to exist. If its state set is empty or no reference satisfies its conditions, the consistency and reference-dependent accuracy clauses can be vacuous. Likewise, admitted-data clauses can be vacuous for families not used by actual cells, although actual and reference admission are explicitly assumed on every executed cell line.

The cell-specific accuracy conclusion has the form exists N, N≤selectedLevel implies estimate. It does not assert that the selected level reaches N. At a fixed selected level this clause alone can be vacuous by choosing a larger N. The separate family-wide estimate does assert a genuine estimate at every sufficiently large family level.

The witnesses p and L in a family estimate may depend on its direction and line, but precede q. C and N may depend on q, but are uniform over all later levels, projected and admitted arrays, E and output indices. Cell-specific p,L may additionally depend on the stage and cell. No common global p,L,C or N across all lines is asserted.
The global error is a maximum-component bound at each cell, with a common scalar bound across cells. It is not a spatial L1, L2 or measure-weighted error estimate.

The input states, physical references and all coefficients are universally supplied. There are no independent sign hypotheses on e_0, a_n, b_n, s_n, ell or r. The norm bounds and positivity of denominators force nonnegativity of the relevant error bounds on executed stages; properties of the selected amplification coefficient require resolving D020's elided choice.

The mass identity retains the sum of right-minus-left numerical fluxes over all cells. No closed-boundary, periodicity, interface-pairing or cancellation assumption reduces this sum to zero in the displayed conclusion.
Line locality means dependence only on cells assigned to the same directional line, together with fixed ghost data. It does not give a fixed-width stencil or dependence on only neighboring cells.
ReferenceOn already assumes the exact directional integral cell balance. Its appearance in the conclusion does not establish this balance from differentiability or from a separately stated PDE.

Q_n is a separate physical field for each stage, with local reference time beginning at zero. Interstage continuity is controlled only through the supplied cell-mean splitting-defect bounds. There is no asserted common global-time physical solution.
The optional Cartesian conclusions are implications for every compatible set of axes and positions. They do not assert that such Cartesian compatibility exists for the supplied geometry.
The abstract measure need not be Lebesgue globally, and Cartesian compatibility equates restricted measures rather than asserting literal equality of abstract cell regions with Cartesian boxes.

The all-field Cartesian mean and lifted face-flux identities quantify even over fields without a new integrability premise. They use the total Lean integral and inverse operations; interpretation as classical normalized integrals requires the relevant integrability. The final all-time conservation statement does impose its own integrability hypotheses.

Hyperbolicity means existence of a real eigenbasis for the state derivative. Distinct characteristic speeds, uniform diagonalization bounds, entropy inequalities, positivity preservation and existence or uniqueness of PDE solutions are not encoded.

The controlled-resolution variation bound permits growth by 1+K dt and a vanishing-noise additive term. It is not a strict nonincrease of total variation, and no separate multidimensional total-variation estimate is concluded.
No asymptotic smallness is assumed for the supplied localDefect or splittingDefect sequences. Consequently the finite recursive error bound alone is not a convergence theorem.
